subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: May a QQ Bot C2C sender implicitly authorize privileged approval actions when the account has no explicit non-wildcard approver configured?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally separates permission to chat from permission to approve privileged operations, while the linked pull request would remove that distinction for every direct conversation; source inspection cannot determine whether QQ's C2C identity contract is strong enough to make that safe.

options.title: Keep explicit approval authority
options.body: Retain the current gate and improve the prompt, setup flow, or diagnostics so operators can configure an explicit approver without waiting for a timeout.

options.title: Bind verified owner identity
options.body: Permit direct approvals only when the callback actor is proven to match a configured or paired owner identity, with focused security tests and live QQ proof.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Accept the linked pull request's blanket direct-conversation bypass and explicitly own the resulting behavior under open DM policies.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit approval authority
recommendation.body: Retain the current gate and improve the prompt, setup flow, or diagnostics so operators can configure an explicit approver without waiting for a timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and helped land the existing QQ approval security gate and are best positioned to decide whether its direct-conversation boundary may change.
